name: CompositionDashboard
title: Templates/Platform/Dashboards/CompositionDashboard
summary: A composition dashboard: how a total breaks down into its parts and how that mix moved over time, here the organization’s monthly spend by category. Under a page heading with the period Select and an Export button sits a row of four StatTiles, the total first and then its three largest categories, each with the change against the previous month and a 12-month sparkline; a rise reads as bad, so every tile is `inverse`. Below, a 12-column grid of ChartCards: the stacked Chart of spend by category over 12 months (Area or Bar from a SegmentedButton, crosshair, one tooltip for every category, a legend with range totals) beside a DonutChart of the current month’s split with the total in its center, and a ranked contributors TableRoot across the full width: rank, the resource name behind its category glyph, the category Tag, the amount, its share of the total as a ProgressBar with the percentage, and the change against last month as a Tag. Built from `StatTile`, `Chart`, `DonutChart`, `ChartCard`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `ProgressBar`, `Hint`, `SegmentedButton`, `Select`, `Dropdown`, `IconButton`, `Button` and `EmptyState`.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: While the first response loads, every tile, both charts and the table hold their place with a Skeleton, so the grid does not reflow when data arrives.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: Nothing was billed in the selected period. The tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, and the stacked chart, the donut and the table each keep their box with an EmptyState that names the reason.
